rv.q: You can't get very deep if you haven't decided where to dig, and Memoirs is aiming all over the place.
A tantalizing morsel of what might have been is Colette and Léon’s duet “Sometimes in the Evening,” which has the slow-burn sexiness of an old Lee Hazlewood-Nancy Sinatra collaboration.
It also boldly places the avant-garde of the erotic imagination on an off-Broadway stage.
In the end, “Memoirs” is worth seeing, not for all its tepid raciness but Sheik’s music, Caruso’s singing and her delightfully furry armpits.
Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen offers an all-encompassing experience and staging that fires on all cylinders.
Though several songs start off promisingly, none of them crept into my bones as quickly as those in 'Spring Awakening' and some from Sheik's other shows did.
I can’t say that the focus allows any deep psychological insights, but it does give each of the principal cast members a time to show off their powerhouse vocals.

The ballad-heavy score is a sharp reminder that Sheik was extremely capable of penning lovely and soaring melodies along with clever yet accessible lyrics (almost all of which are perfect rhymes), which is a rarity in today's musical theater landscape.
As what seems to be his final musical offering, Sheik has written a bold and strong score, but once the songs have ended, they don’t leave many lasting impressions.
Sophia Anne Caruso is the reason to see Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen.
It’s a highly enjoyable evening and a worthwhile experience.
While Memoirs of Amorous Gentlemen captures the look of underground naughtiness, there's nothing particularly sexy on display.

cn.t: Critics offer mixed praise for Duncan Sheik's final musical, lauding his beautiful score and Sophia Anne Caruso's starmaking performance, but finding the sex-work story uneven and struggling to balance its provocative premise with emotional depth.

vr.q: The sexiest show in New York right now is happening in a lavish basement in Chelsea.
I thought everything about this show was great except for the book and the lyrics.
